title: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
statement:
You are given a string `s` made only of the characters `(` and `)`.

A parentheses string is **valid** if every `(` can be matched with a later `)`, every `)` with an earlier `(`, and each character is used in exactly one match. In other words, scanning from left to right the number of `)` never exceeds the number of `(`, and both counts are equal at the end.

In one move you may **insert** a single parenthesis (either kind) at any position of the string. Print the **minimum number of insertions** needed to make `s` valid.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer asked for a solution that uses `O(1)` extra space, so a stack is not acceptable; track a couple of counters instead.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum number of insertions.

examples.explanation: The second `)` has no `(` before it, so one `(` must be added in front. The final `(` has no `)` after it, so one `)` must be added at the end. Total 2.
The `)` at indices 3 and 4 match the `(` at indices 2 and 1. The `(` at index 0 and the `(` at index 5 stay unmatched, so two `)` must be added.
The string is already valid, so nothing needs to be inserted.

hints: Scan from left to right and keep the number of `(` that are still waiting for a `)`.
When you see `)` and nothing is waiting, that `)` can never be matched by what came before; it forces one insertion of a `(`. Count those.
At the end, every `(` still waiting needs one inserted `)`. The answer is the number of unmatched `)` found during the scan plus the number of `(` left waiting.
